paper.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial multi-armed bandit with semi-bandit feedback and smooth index-invariant reward (lower bound)
unmapped: Reward is a known general (possibly nonlinear, non-monotone) differentiable 'smooth index invariant' function r(S;mu) of the means of the selected base arms
Base-arm observations in [0,1] may be correlated within a round
Hard instances are I-disjoint: a common subset I of arms in every action, other arms in exactly one action
Canonical K = number of base arms (paper's m); canonical m = action size (paper's K); learner knows the action size and reward function
settings.definition_quote: Denote the number of arms (`base arms') by $\Narms$, and let $\actionset\subset 2^{\brs*{\Narms}}$ be the set of possible actions ... The number of base arms in each action ... is bounded by $\abs{\action}\le\Nbatch$ ... the arms generate an observation vector $\obs{t}\in\brs*{0,1}^\Narms$, sampled from a fixed distribution independently of other rounds. ... the agent aims to minimize its regret $R(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T\br*{\reward{\action^*}{\meanvec}-\reward{\action_t}{\meanvec}}$

symbols.sum_S_KL: sum over suboptimal actions S of Delta_S / KL(nu_S, nu_{S*}), where nu_S is the joint distribution of the arms in action S

conditions: I-disjoint CMAB problem with |S| = m for all actions
there exists an arm i not in I in S* with nondegenerate distribution and nonzero gradient of r at S*

source.label: lemma:generalDependentBound
source.quote: Let $\rewardNoArgs$ be a smooth index invariant reward function with $\abs*{\action}=\Nbatch$ for all $\action\in\actionset$. Also, let $\unu$ be the action distribution of an $I$-disjoint CMAB problem ... Then, for all consistent strategies $\psi$ and all suboptimal actions $S$, liminf E[N_S(T)]/ln T >= 1/KL(nu_S,nu_{S*}). Specifically, ... liminf E[R(T)]/ln T >= sum_{S:Delta_S>0} Delta_S/KL(nu_S,nu_{S*})

results.notes: Lai-Robbins type bound adapted to I-disjoint CMAB; also gives pull-count bound per action.

symbols.G_dep: max over subsets I of tilde_gamma_g^2(mu;I)/K_I, with tilde_gamma_g the modified Gini-weighted smoothness and K_I = m - |I|

conditions: reward function is smooth index invariant
for any mu in [0,1]^m there exists an I-disjoint instance with E[nu_{S*}] = mu and minimal gap Delta_min (existential instance)

source.label: theorem:dependent_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $\rewardNoArgs$ be a smooth index invariant reward function. For any $\meanvec\in\brs*{0,1}^\Nbatch$ and any small enough $\dr{}>0$, there exists an instance of an $\commset$-disjoint bandit problem $\unu$ with minimal gap $\dr{}$ and $\E\brs*{\nu_{\action^*}}=\meanvec$, such that the expected regret of any consistent algorithm is bounded by liminf E[R(t)]/ln T >= max_I (m-2K) tilde_gamma_g^2(mu;I)/(8 K_I Delta) = DB^*_r(Delta;mu).

results.notes: Paper's m (base arms) mapped to canonical K, paper's K (action size) to canonical m. Combined with Prop. relations, monotone rewards give tilde-Omega(gamma_g^2 m ln T / Delta) (informal); linear and PMC special cases reproduce known bounds.

symbols.M_items: number of summands of the reward tilde r = sum_{i=1}^M r(mu_i)

conditions: reward is a sum of M smooth index-invariant functions over M independent blocks
existential instance with optimal action means mu_i = mu for all blocks

source.label: corollary: sum index invariant dependent
source.quote: Let $\rewardNoArgs$ be a smooth index invariant reward function and let $\tilde\meanvec=\brs*{\meanvec_1,\dots,\meanvec_\Nitems}$ ... define $\tilde{\rewardNoArgs}\br*{\tilde\meanvec} = \sum_{i=1}^\Nitems \rewardvec{\meanvec_i}$. Then ... the expected regret of any consistent algorithm is bounded by liminf E[R(t)]/ln T >= M^2 DB^*_r(Delta;mu).

results.notes: K and m here refer to the per-summand base-arm count and action size.

symbols.KL_nu: KL(nu, nu*) between the suboptimal and optimal action distributions

conditions: nu, nu* agree on arms in I, which are independent of other arms
instance chosen depending on the strategy and T

source.label: lemma:generalIndependentBound
source.quote: ... Then, for any horizon $T$ and any strategy $\psi$, there exists an $\commset$-disjoint CMAB problem with arm distribution $\unu'$ such that $\nu_{\action^*}=\meanvec^*$ and its regret under strategy $\psi$ is bounded by E[R(T)] >= T Delta (1 - K_I/(m-K) - sqrt(1/2 T K_I/(m-K) KL(nu,nu*))).

results.notes: General minimax-style lemma; paper's m/K mapped to canonical K/m.

symbols.G_ind: max over subsets I of tilde_gamma_g(mu;I)/sqrt(K_I), K_I = m - |I|

conditions: reward function is smooth index invariant
K >= 3m (paper: number of base arms >= 3 x action size)
for any mu in [0,1]^m, instance chosen depending on the strategy and T, with E[nu'_{S*}] = mu

source.label: theorem:independent_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $\rewardNoArgs$ be a smooth index invariant reward function and assume that $\Narms\ge3\Nbatch$. Then, for any $\meanvec\in\brs*{0,1}^\Nbatch$, any $T\ge T_0$ and for any strategy $\psi$, there exists an $\commset$-disjoint CMAB problem $\unu'$ with $\E\brs*{\nu'_{\action^*}}=\meanvec$ such that its regret under strategy $\psi$ is bounded by E[R(T)] >= max_I tilde_gamma_g(mu;I)/32 sqrt(T(m-K)/K_I) = IB^*_r(mu).

results.notes: Printed theorem number not visible. Monotone case gives tilde-Omega(gamma_g sqrt(KT)) via propositions (informal).

symbols.M_items: number of summands of the reward

conditions: reward is a sum of M smooth index-invariant functions over independent blocks

source.label: corollary: sum index invariant independent
source.quote: Under the notations of Corollary 7, if $\Narms\ge3\Nbatch$, then for any $\meanvec\in\brs*{0,1}^\Nbatch$, any $T\ge T_0$ and for any strategy $\psi$, there exists CMAB problem $\unu'$ ... whose regret under strategy $\psi$ is bounded by E[R(T)] >= M IB^*_r(mu).
